title: Unbounded evaluation on finitely many clopen geometric sections
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, and put $P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $r:V\to P$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $I$ be a finite set and let $s_i:P\hookrightarrow V$ for $i\in I$ be pairwise disjoint open immersions with closed images [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion], satisfying $rs_i=1_P$. Write $U=\coprod_{i\in I}P$, $j:U\hookrightarrow V$ for their union, and $u=rj:U\to P$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Use constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale sites and the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $K\in D(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, write $K_i=s_i^*Dj_!K$ for its restriction to the $i$-th component, using exact inverse image and degreewise extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. The canonical restriction map gives a natural isomorphism
$$Rr_*Dj_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i\in I}K_i$$
in $D(P_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, where the derived direct image is computed by K-injective resolutions [def-kun-unbounded-exchange, def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. On the clopen decomposition $V=j(U)\amalg(V\setminus j(U))$, a complex is K-injective exactly when its component complexes are K-injective. Thus the displayed isomorphism is normalized by resolutions taken on the $P$ components with zero complex on the complement, followed by the exact global-sections equivalence $\operatorname{Mod}(P_{\mathrm{et}},A)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}_A$ [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk].
Put $B=Du_{\Sigma!}K=\bigoplus_{i\in I}K_i$ using exact etale sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension, lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives]. Define $\delta_K:r^*B\to Dj_!K$ by the projection $\bigoplus_iK_i\to K_i$ on the component $s_i(P)$ and by zero on the complement. Under $r^*\dashv Rr_*$ [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], its adjunct $a_K:B\to Rr_*Dj_!K$ becomes the canonical finite sum-to-product map. In particular $a_K$ is an isomorphism; after the canonical finite biproduct identification it is the identity, including $I=\varnothing$.

proof.text: The finite disjoint union of the section images is open and closed. Prove this using scheme coproduct injections, the finite union of closed sets, and the open-cover criterion for etaleness. Adjoin the open complement to obtain a finite coproduct presentation of V. The empty family is included.

Construct the module-valued clopen equivalence directly by the unit and counit of restriction/direct image: reconstruction is the product of component direct images. The off-diagonal restrictions vanish and each diagonal counit is invertible. The same argument works on the derived categories, since clopen direct image is exact and the derived restriction functors jointly reflect isomorphisms. This is the module-valued version of the finite-clopen product calculation, proved here rather than assuming a lifted abelian-sheaf equivalence. The sole-nonzero-factor projection is the existing Etale.singleProjectionIso from Sheaf.SixFunctors.WeaklyContractibleEtaleConstantModels, exposed for reuse; no duplicate projection theorem is introduced.

K-injectivity restricts to each component by the exact extension/restriction adjunction. Conversely lift the component null homotopies through the fully faithful restriction equivalence; faithfulness proves the homotopy equations. Resolve a complex on U using the existing K-injective-resolution instance and extend the resolution through the clopen immersion. Clopen extension agrees with direct image, hence preserves K-injectivity; its complementary restriction is zero.

For an object with zero complementary restriction, the derived clopen equivalence identifies maps into it with families of maps into its section restrictions. Transport through the canonical derived adjunction r* ⊣ Rr*. Naturality of the section comparison and the counit formula identify this Hom bijection with postcomposition by the stated evaluation map. Yoneda proves evaluation invertible. Its naturality follows from the defining natural transformations. The existing point global-sections equivalence gives the module normalization.

For the exact etale sum adjunction on U, use the component equivalence to identify maps from its value with families of maps from the component restrictions. This proves the coproduct universal property for exactly the injections obtained from the adjunction unit and the section comparison. Transport by the component isomorphisms to Ki; uniqueness of colimits gives e. Naturality of the unit and comparisons proves e natural.

Use full faithfulness of the derived clopen restriction equivalence to construct delta with the prescribed projections and zero complementary component. Faithfulness proves naturality. For its adjunct, the counit identity proved in clopenSectionDerivedRestriction_adj gives each projection equal to e followed by the indicated biproduct projection. Product extensionality gives the required equality. The finite biproduct-to-product comparison and evaluation are isomorphisms, so the adjunct is invertible. All constructions include the empty family.

The blueprint place is main-20261015 prop-asd-smooth-base-change coherence (iii), proof lines 50-56. The statement is true. Directly, RΓ(V,j_!K)=∏RΓ(P,K_i)×RΓ(Z,0) and Γ on P=Spec Ω is exact, so no finiteness of A and no boundedness is needed. The adjunct of δ is b↦(π_i b), the sum-to-product map. Edge cases checked: I empty, Z empty, A=0, A not finite, complexes unbounded in both directions. Step checks: (1) coproduct-family and clopen-product give the exact module equivalence, with the A-action lifted componentwise. (2) j^{-1} is projection and u^{-1} is the diagonal since rs_i=1, and j_!≅(F_i,0) by uniqueness of left adjoints. (3) The Hom complex is a finite product, so K-injectivity is componentwise; this is elementary. (4) J=(J_i,0) is K-injective and r_*J(W)=J(W×_PV)=∏J_i(W), with zero on the complement. (5) Naturality and independence of resolution choices follow from kinjective-hom-derived. (6) u_! is the direct sum by adjoint uniqueness, and δ is represented by (π_i,0). (7) r_*J is K-injective since r^* is exact; the step uses the chain-level formula for the derived adjunction.
